meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_69_packages.json, torah_69_additions.json, torah_69_ce_edges.json, and torah_69.txt. Collected all node IDs already assigned to packages (including additions). Extracted all unique node IDs from cause/effect edges. Identified nodes appearing in cause/effect edges but not in any package. Assigned each unassigned node to the package matching its ESSENTIAL NATURE — what the concept IS at its core, not merely what it causally connects to.

assignments.node_id: אם אין די לך בחלקך, ואתה שונא את ממונך, שאינו מספיק לך, על כן שלח. הינו שתעשה תקנה לזה
assignments.node_text: אִם אֵין דַּי לְךָ בְּחֶלְקְךָ, וְאַתָּה שׂוֹנֵא אֶת מָמוֹנְךָ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַסְפִּיק לְךָ, עַל כֵּן שַׁלַּח. הַיְנוּ שֶׁתַּעֲשֶׂה תַּקָּנָה לָזֶה
assignments.reason: This node describes the prophetic advice (Malachi 2:16): if you are dissatisfied with your portion of wealth and hate your money for being insufficient, 'send forth' — i.e. give tzedakah. Its essential nature is a tikkun (rectification) for the insufficiency of ממון. The concept is entirely about the relationship to one's wealth-portion and the remedy of 'שלח' (sending forth / tzedakah), both of which are core nodes of Package 1. The node describes the positive/corrective orientation toward wealth, hence polarity is good.

assignments.node_id: יוכל לתקן ממון גזלה שיש לו, הינו שגזלו על־ידי חמדה
assignments.node_text: יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן מָמוֹן גְּזֵלָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ, הַיְנוּ שֶׁגְּזָלוֹ עַל־יְדֵי חֶמְדָּה
assignments.reason: This node describes the ability to rectify stolen wealth (ממון גזלה) that was obtained through coveting (חמדה). Its essential nature is about the status and rectification of ממון — specifically wealth that has been tainted by theft-through-coveting. The node refers to ממון in its damaged/tainted state and the possibility of its repair. This is squarely within the ממון domain (Package 1). Polarity is neutral because the node describes a transitional state: the wealth itself is tainted (negative) but the tikkun possibility (positive) is inherent in the statement.

assignments.node_id: יוכל לתקן ממונו, בחינות אשת נעוריו, ולא לבגד בה
assignments.node_text: יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן מָמוֹנוֹ, בְּחִינוֹת אֵשֶׁת נְעוּרָיו, וְלֹא לִבְגֹּד בָּהּ
assignments.reason: Although this node mentions ממון, its essential nature is about rectifying the relationship with אשת נעוריו (the wife of one's youth) — i.e. the nefesh/nekeivah/bat-zug. The phrase 'בחינות אשת נעוריו ולא לבגד בה' explicitly frames the tikkun as restoring fidelity to the feminine soul-dimension. The ממון here is the instrument, but the ESSENCE of what is being described is the restoration of the nefesh-nekeivah bond. This belongs in Package 2 (Soul and the Feminine). Polarity is good: the node describes faithful restoration, not betrayal.

This node describes extracting 'her' (the nefesh/nekeivah) from among the klipot. The source text (line 33) makes clear that the 'her' is the nefesh in its feminine aspect: 'הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַקְּלִפּוֹת עַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ, בְּחִינַת נוּקְבָא, בִּבְחִינַת רַגְלֶיהָ יוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת.' The essential nature of this node is: the rescue of the nefesh-nekeivah from captivity among the klipot. This is a redemption of the feminine soul-dimension, placing it squarely in Package 2 (Soul and the Feminine). Polarity is good: extraction from klipot is a positive/holy act.

assignments.node_id: שיתקים אצלו ממונו, אף שהיא של גזלה על ידי החמדה
assignments.node_text: שֶׁיִּתְקַיֵּם אֶצְלוֹ מָמוֹנוֹ, אַף שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל גְּזֵלָה עַל יְדֵי הַחֶמְדָּה
assignments.reason: This node describes the outcome that one's ממון endures/is sustained even though it was obtained through theft-by-coveting. Its essential nature is about the status and persistence of ממון — specifically, stolen wealth that achieves stability through tzedakah. This is a description of ממון in its rectified-yet-originally-tainted state. The concept is entirely within the ממון domain (Package 1). Polarity is neutral: the wealth is sustained (positive) but its origin is theft-by-coveting (negative); the node captures both poles.

assignments.node_id: שמה שתעשו משפט, ותצילו גזול מיד גוזלו
assignments.node_text: שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁתַּעֲשׂוּ מִשְׁפָּט, וְתַצִּילוּ גָּזוּל מִיַּד גּוֹזְלוֹ
assignments.reason: This node describes the act of executing justice and rescuing the stolen property from the robber's hand. Its essential nature is about the restoration of ממון to its rightful owner — the act of justice (משפט) that reverses the theft of wealth (the branches/ענפים of the victim's tree). In the source text (line 16), this is framed within the ממון framework: robbery takes the victim's branches, and justice restores them. The concept is about restoring the stolen wealth-dimension. Polarity is good: justice/rescue of the robbed is a positive act.

This node describes the outcome of doing good for the children (בנים). Its essential nature is about the welfare of בנים — the children who are the fruits (פרות) of the tree. The source text (line 16) immediately clarifies: 'שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת לִמּוּדֵי ה'' — the children ARE limudei Hashem (Torah-students). This node belongs in Package 3 (Children and Torah) because its essence is about the benefit to children/Torah-students. Polarity is good: doing good for children/limudei Hashem is entirely within the domain of holiness.
